log: Working out who would actually buy this
Discovering candidates and exact source URLs (stage 1 of 2)
Fetching up to 10 exact URLs; validating against at most 48,000 characters
Evaluating candidates against 6 fetched pages (stage 2 of 2)

Search was English-language with no geographic restriction because the supplied scope did not specify either. Public buyer evidence was strongest in personal blogs, public newsletter archives, association minutes, GitHub-oriented handbooks, Reddit, and Patreon community announcements. Searches did not find reliable public population counts, a confirmed Buttondown Teams purchase by a growing editorial team, a weekend-support SLA, a reconciled Teams pricing explanation, or complete base subscriber-tier pricing above 100. The Turing Way publication guide appears internally stale because it says Buttondown is currently used while later steps still name TinyLetter; it is used only as workflow evidence, not as proof of a current Buttondown configuration.
